name: Tower Bridge
locality: London Borough of Tower Hamlets, London Borough of Southwark
type: suspension bridge; road bridge; bascule bridge; gothic revival bridge; steel bridge
text: Tower Bridge is a Grade I listed combined bascule, suspension, and, until 1960, cantilever bridge in London, built between 1886 and 1894, designed by Horace Jones and engineered by John Wolfe Barry with the help of Henry Marc Brunel. It crosses the River Thames close to the Tower of London and is one of five London bridges owned and maintained by the City Bridge Foundation, a charitable trust founded in 1282. The bridge was constructed to connect the 39% of London's population that lived east of London Bridge, equivalent to the populations of "Manchester on the one side, and Liverpool on the other", while allowing shipping to access the Pool of London between the Tower of London and London Bridge.

depictions.name: Tower Bridge
depictions.text: Tower Bridge is a combined bascule and suspension bridge located in central London. Built from 1886 to 1894, the bridge crosses the River Thames close to the Tower of London, which it takes its name from.
